THE OWNER'S CONTRACT, verbatim intent: full automation, never skip steps; if a step is not needed, an artifact must say WHY it was skipped, and a process must manage that.

EXTERNAL REVIEW FINDINGS driving this change (Codex verifier, 2026-07-31):
  * "audit_run() reports optional omissions as strings, with no reason, applicability rule, artifact path, hash, timestamp, or authorization. Wiring this function alone would not satisfy the owner's skip-artifact requirement." (episode_dag.py ~line 334)
  * "The graph collapses all four promotion emails into one optional promo_email step and ends at promo_schedule; it contains no distinct warmup, tease, launch, follow-up, referral-ask, referral-follow-up, or public-readback lifecycle steps." (episode_dag.py ~line 108)

THE CHANGE, two parts:

PART 1 — SKIP ARTIFACTS AS FIRST-CLASS OBJECTS.
1. Define SKIP_REASON_CODES, a bounded vocabulary (extendable deliberately, never free-text-only), at minimum: not_applicable, superseded_by, owner_waived, upstream_unavailable, policy_gate. Free text goes in a separate "detail" field; the CODE is what a process can manage.
2. make_skip_artifact(step_id, *, reason_code, detail, authorized_by, now, evidence=None) -> dict
   Returns the canonical skip artifact: {"schema":"episode-skip-v1", "step_id", "reason_code",
   "detail", "authorized_by", "skipped_at" (iso from `now`), "evidence" (list), and
   "content_hash" (sha256 over the sorted canonical JSON of the other fields, so a skip
   artifact cannot be silently edited without the hash changing).
   Raise ValueError on an unknown reason_code, empty authorized_by, or empty detail —
   an unexplained or unowned skip is exactly what the owner has banned.
3. validate_skip_artifact(artifact) -> list[str] of problems; empty means valid. It must
   recompute and check the content_hash. A tampered or schema-less artifact is invalid.
4. audit_run gains a skip_artifacts parameter (mapping step_id -> artifact). Semantics:
   * A required step that did not run and has NO valid skip artifact: run is INCOMPLETE and
     the report names it as a SILENT skip (the banned case).
   * A required step that did not run but has a VALID skip artifact: named in the report as
     an AUTHORIZED skip with its reason_code and authorizer; does not make complete False.
   * An INVALID artifact (bad hash, unknown code) is worse than none: report it as
     "invalid skip artifact" and keep the run incomplete — a forged or corrupted
     authorization must never count.
   * Optional steps unchanged: named, never blocking.

PART 2 — THE DAG COVERS THE FULL LIFECYCLE.
Split and extend the graph so every real external effect is its own step:
  promo_email_warmup, promo_email_tease, promo_email_launch, promo_email_followup
  (replacing the single promo_email step; read the orchestrator's actual unit names —
  publish_units uses promo_email:<stage>:<addr> — and mirror those stages);
  referral_ask (after publish; the system asking the guest for referrals),
  referral_followup (after referral_ask),
  social_schedule (the three-touch week plan, requires certification per the owner's
  schedule-at-certification rule: it must NOT require publish, only certification),
  public_readback (verifying the published artifacts are actually live and consistent;
  requires publish).
Keep guest_assets as a requirement of thumbnail and show_notes (tests already pin this).
Declare requirements honestly from the code you can see; where behaviour is genuinely
policy-gated (emails behind the autonomy ladder), the step exists and a skip artifact with
reason_code policy_gate is the correct representation of "gated today" — encode that in a
test so the pattern is demonstrated.

TESTS (tests/test_skip_artifacts.py; at least 7):
 (1) a required step skipped with NO artifact -> incomplete, named as SILENT;
 (2) the same skip with a VALID artifact (owner_waived, authorized_by set) -> complete,
     named as AUTHORIZED with code and authorizer;
 (3) NEGATIVE: a tampered artifact (mutate detail after creation) fails validate and the
     run stays incomplete, reported as invalid — forged authorization never counts;
 (4) NEGATIVE: make_skip_artifact raises on unknown reason_code, empty detail, empty
     authorized_by;
 (5) the four promo email steps exist as distinct DAG steps matching the orchestrator's
     stage names, and referral_ask/referral_followup/social_schedule/public_readback exist;
 (6) social_schedule requires certification and does NOT require publish;
 (7) a policy_gate skip artifact on promo_email_warmup yields a complete run with the gate
     named — the "gated today" pattern;
 (8) determinism: identical inputs give identical reports.
Keep tests/test_episode_dag.py green; update the E104 replay test if step renames affect it,
with a one-line comment.
